answer: Delayed-Identity Horizon Lock.** New agents stay in a probation pool and cannot transact as full peers until a fixed wall-clock horizon passes; their actions emit a verifiable signal only after that delay. Each identity carries a per-day upkeep drawn from its own pool, so clone upkeep accrues during the waiting tide before any earning power unlocks. Attacker cost: pay upkeep for N identities across the full horizon with zero revenue, making each marginal clone strictly negative-EV.
